metadata.concept_name: ZeroFizz Sugar-Free Carbonated Beverage - Means-End Chain
metadata.product_name: ZeroFizz Sugar-Free Carbonated Beverage - Means-End Chain
metadata.objective: Explore how health-conscious adults 18-35 navigate sugar-free carbonated beverage choices — from concrete product attributes (zero-sugar sweetener identity, caffeine dose, carbonation intensity, can design, price per 12-pack, availability at their usual grocery) to the functional consequences they produce (no 2pm crash, alertness without jitters, satisfying the soda craving without calories) to the psychosocial consequences they enable (feeling in control, belonging at a rooftop bar without a cocktail, signaling a modern wellness identity without preaching) to the deeper values these consequences serve (autonomy over ingredient choices, vitality, authenticity in lifestyle signaling, belonging with peers who are cutting back on alcohol, pragmatism over purity). Treat category alternatives — Coke Zero, LaCroix, Celsius — as contrast references when respondents describe why a given attribute led them to choose or reject a product.

turns.question: So I'm really curious about the fizzy drinks you actually reach for — like, when you're in your kitchen or at a store, what are you grabbing these days, and what's going through your head when you make that choice?
turns.response: Honestly I've been grabbing more of the sugar-free stuff lately. I used to just grab whatever was there but I started thinking more about like, not wanting the crash after, you know? So now it's usually something with zero sugar if I can find it that doesn't taste completely awful.

turns.question: What other things about ZeroFizz matter to you besides the zero sugar part?
turns.response: Honestly the taste is pretty important. Like, I've had other diet drinks that taste kind of off, and ZeroFizz doesn't really have that artificial sweetener aftertaste that bugs me. That's probably the main thing.
